title: Credential backfill latency lets stale sessions preserve elevated roles
creator: Ethan Morrison
description: Production bug: during credential backfill after a metadata DB failover, the session reconciliation path allowed previously revoked API keys to continue authorizing requests for a short window. This caused transient preservation of elevated org roles for some Dedicated and Private customers. The issue manifests only when backfill latency overlaps with session lease refresh and the edge proxy accepts stale session cache entries. Customers reported short-lived authorization anomalies (reads allowed post-revocation).
impact: Several Dedicated and Private customers observed transient access to org-scoped resources after API key revocation/backfill during DB failover. Estimated affected customers: 3 large customers; user-facing errors included confused permission checks and one customer reported audit log discrepancies. Window duration observed: ~30–120s depending on failover and backfill throughput.
replication_steps: 1) Simulate metadata DB primary->standby failover in a Dedicated region with active session cache enabled
2) Trigger credential backfill job that reconciles API key bindings from authoritative store
3) Revoke an API key mid-backfill and perform a request against a protected org-scoped endpoint
4) Observe that edge node accepts the request when session lease refresh races with backfill write; session cache TTL keeps stale binding until reconciliation completes
root_cause: Edge session reconciliation path assumes backfill writes are atomic and immediately visible. During failover, backfill batching and a background backfill worker produced delayed writes; meanwhile session refresh used a local fast-path cache and did not verify authoritative binding when refresh occurred concurrently. Result: stale session binding persisted through short window.
mitigation: Hotfix: On edge auth path, add authoritative binding double-check for any session refresh that occurs within 2 minutes of a metadata DB failover event (deployed as feature-flagged check)
Operational: Notify Dedicated/Private customers about scheduled maintenance and avoid backfills during customer critical windows until fix is in place
Rollback plan: If hotfix causes regressions, revert feature flag and apply tighter maintenance window controls
fix_plan: Short term (this sprint): implement and roll out feature-flagged authoritative-binding double-check in edge (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14208)
Canary: route 5% traffic in a single Dedicated zone for 2 hours, monitor traces and auth-deny rates
Long term: rework backfill to emit tombstone events and make backfill idempotent with stronger write-through guarantees; add explicit backfill-complete signal to edge cache invalidation
Release target: runtime-1.52 (canary 2026-03-16, full rollout 2026-03-20 pending canary success)
qa_checks: Unit tests for concurrent refresh/backfill race
Integration test: simulated DB failover + backfill + revoke sequence asserting immediate deny after revoke
E2E staging run with synthetic customer workload to validate no authorization regressions
Load test: backfill throughput at production scale with edge validation enabled
follow_up: Add 'backfill-complete' event into cache invalidation pipeline (RFC in docs repo)
Policy: avoid running full credential backfills during cross-region failovers or implement pre-checks
Audit: reconcile affected customers' audit logs and provide incident summary to each customer support lead
Security review: schedule formal review for authoritative-binding double-check logic
